subject: Ephemeral cache handling and certification - proposed redlines
messages:
From: Lina Gomez <l.gomez@aurumhealth.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: Claire Benson <cbenson@henderson-llp.com>, data-privacy@aurumhealth.com
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on ephemeral cache and certification for onshore wipe

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for sending over the draft DPA redlines. We reviewed the section on data retention and had one open question before we proceed to our security team: how does Redwood treat ephemeral cache (KV cache, prefix cache) that may contain fragments of customer prompts or model responses? Specifically: 

- Do you consider ephemeral caches to be "processed data" subject to the same erasure window as persistent storage?
- Do you provide a certification of deletion for cached content when a customer requests erasure or when the onshore wipe is triggered?

The current language in clause 4.2 seems to treat "logs and caches" separately but is vague on timelines and whether backups that are created during KV flushes are covered. Our auditors will want firm timelines and a mechanism for certification.

Can you point us to the operational playbook or propose wording that would satisfy our compliance reviewers? Attaching our suggested phrasing as a starting point.

Best,
Lina
Senior Privacy Manager, Aurum Health
[Attachment: Aurum_DPA_Redline_v1.docx (31KB)]

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Lina Gomez <l.gomez@aurumhealth.com>
Cc: Claire Benson <cbenson@henderson-llp.com>, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on ephemeral cache and certification for onshore wipe

Hi Lina — thanks for the clear notes and the proposed wording. Quick summary up front: we treat ephemeral caches as transient inference artifacts that are not persisted long-term, but we agree they should be addressed explicitly in the DPA. We can accept firm erasure windows for caches and provide a deletion certification tied to the onshore wipe process with limited exceptions for in-flight backups.

Key points in our proposed redline (high level):
- Ephemeral cache (including KV cache and prefix cache) will be retained only for a maximum of 48 hours from generation under normal operating conditions.
- Where an on-demand erasure is requested, Redwood will purge live cache entries within 24 hours and will confirm completion via a signed certificate within 5 business days.
- If a cache entry was included in a transient backup snapshot created for active load-balancing or failover within the 48-hour window, Redwood will delete the associated snapshot at the next scheduled snapshot cycle and include the snapshot identifier in the deletion certificate; exceptions apply if retention is required for an active legal hold.

Operational references: we have an internal playbook that documents the cache purge job, snapshot indexing, and the certification workflow. I attached the sanitized playbook excerpt (ephemeral-cache-playbook.pdf) to show sequence and controls.

Below is a proposed DPA clause you can consider inserting in clause 4.2 (plain-text for review):

"Ephemeral Cache and Transient Artifacts. Supplier maintains ephemeral inference caches (including but not limited to KV caches and prefix caches) that are necessary to fulfill low-latency inference. Unless otherwise required by law or legal hold, Supplier retains ephemeral cache entries for no longer than forty-eight (48) hours following creation. Upon Customer's verifiable erasure request, Supplier shall purge live ephemeral cache entries associated with the Customer within twenty-four (24) hours and issue a deletion certification to Customer within five (5) business days. Any transient snapshot or backup created in the ordinary course to support high-availability may be deleted at the time of the next scheduled snapshot rotation; Supplier will include identifiers of such snapshots in the deletion certification where applicable."
We believe this addresses auditors' need for timelines and a certification mechanism while allowing operational flexibility for HA snapshots. Happy to iterate.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Senior Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ephemeral-cache-playbook.pdf (14KB)]

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: internal: suggested tightening to deletion certification window

Soojin — a few quick notes from legal/PS perspective after reading Lina's ask and your draft:

- Suggest tightening the certification delivery to 3 business days rather than 5 for enterprise healthcare customers; auditors often flag 5 days as "too loose."
- Propose adding a short definition for "transient snapshot" to avoid ambiguity about what must be listed in the certificate. Something like: "Transient snapshot: a point-in-time copying of live KV or memory-resident artifacts created for failover or scaling and not stored beyond the snapshot rotation window."
- Recommend we explicitly exclude ephemeral telemetry (scheduler logs, GUIDs used for routing) from the deletion certification unless such telemetry contains customer-provided content.

If we tighten to 3 days, we should expect some internal process tweaks (shorter certificate prep and an automated snapshot-ID extraction). I can draft a redline to circulate.

— Jasmine
Senior Product Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Claire Benson <cbenson@henderson-llp.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, Lina Gomez <l.gomez@aurumhealth.com>
Cc: data-privacy@aurumhealth.com
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 16:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Ephemeral cache handling and certification - proposed redlines

Thanks — Claire here (Aurum's outside counsel). We reviewed Redwood's proposed clause and the playbook excerpt. Aurum's priorities are clarity and auditability. A few requested edits: 

1) Please change "within twenty-four (24) hours" to "within forty-eight (48) hours" for purging live cache on customer request to allow for operational variance across regions.
2) We accept the inclusion of snapshot identifiers in the deletion certificate, but request a minimal certificate template (snapshot id, purge timestamp, cert issuer) be included as an appendix to the DPA or provided by Redwood on request.
3) Also request that the certification include the name and role of the person issuing the certificate (or an automated system ID) for chain-of-custody.

Subject to these edits and confirmation that legal hold overrides are respected, Aurum is comfortable approving this language for inclusion.

Claire Benson
Partner, Henderson LLP
